---
title: "Command line"
description: "The studyflow command: convert, check, run, inspect and export a study."
---

## Install

```bash
# Homebrew asks this of a third-party tap
brew trust https://github.com/behaverse/studyflow-modeler
brew tap behaverse/studyflow https://github.com/behaverse/studyflow-modeler
brew install studyflow
```

## Commands

| Command | Does |
|:--|:--|
| [`convert`](#convert) | writes a study in another format |
| [`validate`](#validate) | checks a study without running it |
| [`info`](#info) | shows what a file contains |
| [`run`](#run) | runs a study |
| [`ui`](#ui) | opens the desktop app |
| [`mcp`](#mcp) | serves a study to an AI assistant |
| [`prov`, `crate`, `ocel`](#exports) | export a run's record |
| [`skill`](#skill) | installs, lists and removes skills |

`<input>` is a study as `.studyflow.yaml`, `.bpmn` or `.xml`, `.studyflow.png`, `.studyflow.svg` or `.studyflow.tif`. `studyflow <command> --help` lists every option; the tables below show the main ones.

## convert {#convert}

```bash
studyflow convert <input> <output>
```

The output's extension picks the format (YAML, BPMN XML, PNG, SVG, TIFF). The input can be any of those formats. If the input and output are both images, the output is a copy of the input's pixels.

| Option | Description |
|:--|:--|
| `--image <image>` | embeds the study into this image |
| `--strict` | fails on warnings |

```bash
studyflow convert study.studyflow.yaml study.bpmn
studyflow convert study.studyflow.yaml study.studyflow.png
studyflow convert study.studyflow.png study.studyflow.tif    # the same pixels as the TIFF
```

## validate {#validate}

```bash
studyflow validate <input> [--strict]
```

Reports errors and warnings, and fails on an error. `--strict` fails on a warning too.

## info {#info}

```bash
studyflow info <input> [--json]
```

## run {#run}

```bash
studyflow run <input> [options]
```

Runs the study in the runtime it declares (`local` unless set). A local run first applies the `validate`. [Reference](reference.qmd#running) explains what happens.

| Option | Does |
|:--|:--|
| `--runtime <local\|browser>` | overrides the study's own runtime environment |
| `--author <name>` | who runs it, as git writes an author (`'Name <email>'`) |
| `--repo <dir>` | the run repository to write into (default: the study's directory when it is one, else `~/.studyflow/runs/<name>`) |
| `--from <ref>` | re-runs from this commit, on a branch |
| `--fresh` | ignores earlier runs and re-runs everything |
| `--concurrency <n>` | how many instances of a pool walk at once (default 1) |
| `--runner <name=command>` | adds or replaces a runner for this run; multiple `--runner` options are allowed |
| `--debug` | enables debugging and keeps `.cache/`, with the values after each step |

## ui {#ui}

```bash
studyflow ui [file]
```

Opens the modeler from this machine in offline mode, with the study in `<file>` or a blank canvas. It uses Chrome, Chromium, Brave or Edge, and falls back to the default browser.

## mcp {#mcp}

```bash
studyflow mcp <file>
```

Serves a study, in YAML or BPMN XML, to an AI assistant as a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server on stdio. A modeler GUI with the same file open shows all the changes to accept or discard.

## prov, crate, ocel {#exports}

Provenance, RO-Crate and OCEL exports of a run.

```bash
studyflow prov <run> [out.ttl]                      # W3C PROV-O, in Turtle
studyflow crate <run> <folder> --license CC-BY-4.0  # a Workflow Run RO-Crate
studyflow ocel <run> [out.json]                     # OCEL 2.0, for process mining
```

`<run>` is a run repository or its `events.jsonl`. `crate` needs `--license`, an SPDX id or a URL.

## skill {#skill}

```bash
studyflow skill add <git-or-folder>
studyflow skill list
studyflow skill remove <name>
```

Installs a skill into `~/.studyflow/skills` (or `$STUDYFLOW_HOME/skills`), where every command and the desktop app find it. Adding a skill of the same name replaces it.
